notes:
Summary: pursuing Dedicated capacity with SLA-backed throughput guarantees for real-time personalization and reranking. Primary ask is a committed minimum tokens/sec at P50/P95 on a model family (LlamaX-13B variant) with clear concurrency caps and a defined burst policy. Key negotiation points and account color: 
- RTO: wants 99ms p95 for single-turn personalization requests (typical prompt size ~120 tokens).
- Throughput ask: target baseline 400k tokens/sec sustained across a reserved pool (estimated 12 GPUs), ability to handle short bursts up to 1.2M tokens/sec for 2-3 minutes (3x baseline).
- Concurrency: target hard concurrency cap per-customer = 250 active request slots; soft throttling above 200 with graceful queuing.
- Burst policy: prefer configurable burst credit bucket tied to reserve (e.g., 3x sustained for up to 180s), automatic fallback to smaller / cheaper model family if sustained beyond budget.
- Fallback & routing: application requires deterministic fallback with <150ms additional latency; prefer model variant routing (13B -> 7B) rather than full-deny.
- Cost sensitivity: high; will accept higher committed ARR if predictable unit economics and clear autoscale/burst billing rules.
- Security: VPC deployment, bring-your-own-key (KMS) mandatory, SOC2 + ISO27001 preferred, audit logging exported to their SIEM.
- POC notes: initial POC saturated KV cache benefits, batching improved unit cost by ~22% but increased p95 by 10-15ms; team wants formalized cache hit SLAs in contract.
- Legal asks: MSA addendum to include throughput SLA credits (service credits), precise measurement methodology (how tokens/sec is measured and by which monitoring agent), and runbook for incident with RTO/RPO for inference failures.
- Quote from CTO (paraphrased): "We need guarantees we can plan capacity against — burst behavior and billing clarity are must-haves."
Open items: concrete min tokens/sec number to include in MSA (engineering to provide load model by 2025-11-20), agreed measurement window (1-minute sliding vs 5-minute), and explicit fallback model list.
Recommended Redwood playbook: offer a tiered SLA (baseline committed tokens/sec + burst credits), include automatic model-fallback policy, provide a sample billing calc for burst consumption, deliver a security packet (SOC2 + KMS flow) and sample MSA clause for throughput credits.
Next immediate actions: SE to produce technical appendix with GPU count mapping and expected p95 latency per model variant (due 2025-11-18); Legal to draft SLA wording; AE to schedule follow-up with Finance week of 2025-11-17.
